title: Story 5.9's load-bearing 'surge still lands' acceptance has no pinned test; the golden re-bless would silently bless non-landing
evidence:
stories-v2.md (card 5.9 Then-clause): "~0.2); era-3 demand + 5.1 growth pacing are **re-validated together** so the MVP surge still
  lands (silent non-landing is a fail, not a feature)." — and the same card's Golden line: "**Golden:** T1 (spawn sequence shift — **deliberate, cause-documented re-bless** per the
  4.3 discipline; byte-verify `.log.bin` differs only in the version field, splice the old
  catalog_hash, cause-document); existing goldens unshifted at the const level." Meanwhile core/demand_test.odin (existing test, unnamed by the card) pins exact volumes: "want_stream := u64(2*399 + 20*200 + 2*201)
	testing.expectf(t, by_class[1] == want_stream, "streaming volume (surge x10): got %d, want %d", by_class[1], want_stream)"
detail: The card's own named failure mode (surge silently stops landing) is undetectable as specified: a re-bless byte-blesses whatever the new volumes are, and no scenario or @(test) asserts post-cap surge volume. Project canon: acceptance criteria become durable tests, not PR prose.
recommended_fix: In card 5.9, pin the assertion: extend test_director_surge_amplifies_class (or a new @(test)) to assert, on a map with ≥(20÷cap) streaming sources, spawn volume equals surge rate during the window.

title: Story 5.10's Thread-1 headroom invariant ('access link never congests from one subscriber') is unpinned — re-bless only, no named test or golden scenario
evidence:
stories-v2.md (card 5.10): "- **Then** the narrow access link carries it with **~1.3–1.5× headroom** (cap ≈ 6 u/s vs narrow
  ~8–10 u/s) — the access link never congests from the one subscriber; ..." — then: "unchanged. **Golden:** T1/T2 re-bless (cause-documented, the slice boundary's legitimate re-bless).
- **Launchable increment:** run the app — a single residential on a narrow never drops its own
  traffic; stress appears when many homes share a link." Contrast card 5.11: "**Golden:** T1/T2 re-bless + a T2 frame with all three types visible." and 5.12: "**Golden:** T1/T2 re-bless + a T2 frame of a clustered topology
  under surge (drops at the uplink)."
detail: The mechanic's core player-facing promise has only a manual launchable check; re-blessed existing demos assert nothing about one-subscriber-on-narrow. Cards 5.11/5.12 each name a new pinning scenario — 5.10 uniquely omits one.
recommended_fix: Add to 5.10 a pinning golden/test: a T1 scenario (or @(test)) with a residential sourcing at its cap over one narrow — assert zero serialization/spawn drops at the access link.

title: The SLA accounting identity demand_seen == delivered + dropped + live is miscited as '(E24)'; arch E24 is a different contract
evidence:
spec-traffic-model.md: "The invariant `demand_seen == delivered + dropped + live`
(E24) must hold under both paths — the card pins it with a test." vs odin-architecture-v1.md §11.7: "| E24 | Zero-demand class = neutral SLA | accumulator guard |". The identity's real home is core/sla_test.odin:88-89: "// sla_check_invariant — the pinned accounting identity, every live row.
sla_check_invariant :: proc(t: ^testing.T, s: ^Run_State) {"
detail: Cards 5.9 and the spec attach the wrong E-number to the invariant a minion must extend; following the tag lands on zero-demand-neutral, not the identity helper. Traceability defect, coverage itself is intact.
recommended_fix: Cite the identity by its actual pin (core/sla_test.odin sla_check_invariant) rather than '(E24)', or add the identity to the §11.7 registry before implementation.
